svg:
How the gimbal assembles Doc 3 stage 7 · Doc 3b build order — printed parts, motors, and the DLH-3UP-EH LED housing, pulled apart along both axes
1 Clamp the pan base to a shelf edge Its ear goes under the C-clamp; the plate hangs past the edge. The shelf plays “ceiling.”
2 Hang the pan motor Motor body bolts UP against the plate (4× M3). Its output flange faces DOWN.
3 Bolt the yoke to the pan flange Flange disc, 4× M3 — arms hang down. Pan now swings the whole yoke. Check full travel clears the motor body.
4 Arm the tilt axis Tilt motor body slides into the motor-arm collar, flange facing IN. The 608 bearing presses into the far arm.
5 Mount the head shell Disc bolts to the tilt flange (4× M3). Then the M8 axle bolt slides through the bearing from outside into the end plate — the head is now held on BOTH sides.
6 Slide in the LED housing, balance The aluminum housing (it IS the star's heatsink) glides through the pinch cradle — its barrel CROSSES the tilt axis. Slide it until the powered-OFF head stays posed anywhere, then nip the M3 pinch bolt. M5 nuts on the tail = fine trim. Balance is the silence mechanism.
Axes — pan: vertical · tilt: horizontal (thin gray lines). Cradle ID = housing Ø0.99" + 0.6 mm ≈ 1.014" — a slide fit on purpose. Hardware: 12× M3 at the flanges (the fit coupon proves the pattern first) · 1× M3 pinch bolt · 1× M8 axle bolt · M5 + nuts for trim. Wires: out the housing's rear NPT bore, then droopy service loops.
